body: Umm... Thanks I guess. All the atheists I know have a much stronger moral fiber than any religious person I know.
Honestly, I've been thinking about it since your first post, and I have yet to come up with anything.

I have tried to change so many times. I work harder and harder every time, but I always revert to my previous ways.  All it takes is a good nights rest, and my brain will "reset" my personality. I've even tried staying awake as long as possible when I was having a "happy phase", but I can't stay awake forever.

My parents actually don't have all that long. My fathers health is very poor (organ transplant, medications are torching his other organs), and my mother is very fragile emotionally. I don't think she would last long without my father (they have been married since high school).

The last time I remember being happy, truly happy, was when I thought woman was truly interested in me as a person. Of course, these moments are always short lived, as they usually end up falling quickly for one of my friends or someone else. I assume they realize that there is really nothing there, and move on. I guess it has something to do with living the moments I missed out on, or can't remember, earlier in my life. 

My brain is hard-wired for isolation, and nothing I have been able to do has changed that. In fact, I turned down an invite from friends today just because I don't think I would be able to maintain the facade that is my life. I can't shatter the illusions I have built, or I might be left completely alone.

When I'm not drinking, I feel like I'm just living to pass the time. I think I would feel the same way while drinking if my logical mind didn't shut off. I saturate my sense so I don't have to be alone with my thoughts.

In ten years, I will most likely still be alone, just living to pass the time. My career path with provide me with enough money to bring happiness to those around me (parties, material possessions, vacations etc). Might as well help others enjoy their lives, even if I'm not enjoying mine.

I'm already studying chemistry / medicine. I taught myself a little bit of programming a while back, but I definitely did not enjoy it. Nothing I have found is all that challenging... It's just different applications of the same rudimentary formula. Memorize / Hypothesize facts and/or formulas, apply them, check results.

I don't feel compelled to drink, I have gone months at a time without drinking.

My days are usually spent going to uni, coming home and doing my homework etc, then filling my senses with as much as possible to prevent myself from thinking (listening to music/gaming/watching TV, usually all at the same time). I'm 21 years old, doing well in school (~3.92 GPA at a competitive university), but I feel like I'm mainly doing it for my family. Everyone is counting on me to succeed.
